title: Fixerloop
tagline: Rescuing a services marketplace its own founder found confusing
summary: Fixerloop connects homeowners with professional service providers. The founder came to me because the app was too complicated to use — clashing colours, unclear copy, and a flow he could not defend. I rebuilt it around a proper component library and a design system.

sections.heading: Intro
sections.body: Fixerloop connects homeowners with service providers through a platform meant to be efficient, transparent and easy to use. I met the founder and we went through where the application was falling short. After research, the thing he kept returning to was that the design had to become genuinely user-friendly before anything else was worth doing.

sections.heading: The problem
sections.body: The app was too complicated for users to understand. The colours did not work together. The text was unclear in places, and the whole thing was not simple to use. The founder was not convinced his own application was easy for a customer — which is about as direct a brief as you can get.

sections.heading: The solution
sections.body: We tested, worked to understand where people were actually getting stuck, and rebuilt for clarity. The platform connects professional service providers with clients who need work done across several fields, so the design had to hold two distinct users — the customer looking for someone, and the provider managing requests and orders — without either flow feeling like an afterthought bolted onto the other.

images.alt: Customer home screen headed 'What are you looking for today?', with a service search field and horizontal rows of nearby and popular providers showing verified badges and star ratings
images.caption: Customer home. Search first, then providers near you, each carrying a verification badge and rating.

images.alt: Explore screen listing service categories: Electronics Repair, IT and Telecommunication, HVAC, Cleaning, Pest Control, Interior Decoration and Garden
images.caption: Browsing by category, for people who don't know what to search for.

images.alt: Electronics Repair provider list, each row showing the provider name, distance, a verified badge, a colour-coded rating and a favourite heart
images.caption: Provider list. Distance, verification and rating are the three things that decide a hire.

images.alt: Customer orders list where every row carries a status label reading Pending, Hired or Finished
images.caption: Order states are labelled in words and colour, so status never has to be inferred.

images.alt: Service provider home screen showing an empty state explaining that a full company profile is required to be visible to customers, with a button to complete it
images.caption: The provider empty state does one job: explain why the profile matters, then offer the single next step.

images.alt: Provider requests list, each row showing the customer name, the job with a reference number, and the requested date and time
images.caption: Incoming requests, each identified by job reference and time.

sections.heading: A component library underneath
sections.body: The rebuild sits on a real design system rather than a set of drawn screens: verified and unverified provider cards, provider list rows, rating and star components, message list items and chat bubbles for both sides of a conversation, order and request states including in-progress, primary buttons with icon variants, badges, and a full status-bar and navigation set. That is the reason the app holds together as flows were added — the consistency comes from the system, not from discipline applied screen by screen.

images.alt: Company profile screen assembled from the shared form, card and badge components
images.caption: A dense screen built entirely from shared components.

images.alt: The app's bottom tab bar component showing Home, Explore, My orders and Profile
images.caption: The tab bar as a single reusable component, shared by both customer and provider apps.

sections.heading: The outcome
sections.body: Welcome and signup, customer home and explore, browsing and filtering service providers, the full provider profile with ratings and verification, provider-side orders and requests, and an in-progress order with chat.
